newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Britain will work for Cyprus, says Labour official.
newsitem.headline: Britain will work for Cyprus, says Labour official.

text.p: Britain will raise the profile of the Cyprus question on the international agenda if a Labour government is elected in general elections due this year, a key member of the British opposition party said on Friday.

"The Labour government will have excellent opportunities to ensure that the Cyprus question figures prominently on the agenda of the international community," shadow foreign secretary Robin Cook told a news conference in Nicosia, the divided capital of the eastern Mediterranean island.
General elections must take place in Britain before May 22. The ruling Conservatives trail Labour by around 20 points in opinion polls.
International mediators have recently stepped up efforts to broker a settlement to reunite the Greek and Turkish Cypriots on Cyprus, divided after a Turkish invasion in 1974.
Greece, Turkey and Britain, as the former colonial power, are guarantors of Cyprus under its 1960 independence treaty.
Cook said Labour supported Cyprus's bid to become a member of the European Union, which it is scheduled to start accession talks with in approximately one year.
"Talks on enlargement will probably start during the British presidency in 1998, and as the government of Britain we will be instrumental that they do (start)," he said.
Turkey occupied northern Cyprus in 1974 after a brief coup engineered by the military ruling in Greece at the time.

United Nations-led efforts have so far failed to achieve a breakthrough which would allow Cyprus's reunification under a federal system while the pressure is on both sides to reach an agreement before Cyprus starts entry talks with Europe.
Diplomats are now focusing their efforts on bridging key disputes between the two sides which will allow direct negotiations early this year.
Cook said there was sufficient basis for negotiations to start.
"I do not think it helps to set preconditions for talks. It is not helpful for either side to say 'that and that must be agreed before we start'", he said.
